items.title: Exercise 1.7: justify the noncompact log-Sobolev test

source.anchor: Section 2.1.1, printed pp. 48–49 / PDF pp. 60–61; compact-test LSI and density extension; consumer Exercise 1.7, printed p. 43 / PDF p. 55
source.attribution: Chewi states the compact smooth test inequality and refers to density for extension. The explicit analytic domain and proof below are an original sufficient ASTIS reconstruction, not a quoted theorem or the maximal closed form domain.

items.statement: Starting with function-form LSI on compact smooth tests, retain its constant on smooth tests with square-integrable function and genuine gradient and integrable square-log-square. In a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space the radial cutoff products are valid compact smooth tests. The three integral limits used by this extension also hold in a complete real Hilbert space without finite dimension or a finite-measure assumption.
assumptions: The compact-test inequality is given for every smooth compactly supported test on the finite-dimensional Borel carrier; the coefficient 2C is fixed independently of the test and cutoff.
The extended test is smooth, with f and its genuine gradient in L2 and f^2 log(f^2) in L1. Its sign and total square mass are unrestricted.
The cutoff-limit prerequisite by itself needs only C2 regularity and a complete real Hilbert/Borel carrier. No probability, local finiteness, or finite dimension is needed for those limits.

units.title: Cutoffs preserve the limiting mass, entropy integrand and true gradient energy
units.statement: Let mu be an arbitrary measure on a complete real Hilbert/Borel space. For real C2 f with f and its true gradient in L2(mu) and Phi(f^2) in L1(mu), let f_n be f times the radial cutoff at radius n+1. Then the mass, entropy-integrand and squared-gradient integrals of f_n converge to those of f. Neither a finite measure nor finite dimension is required.
units.formula: f_n=\chi_{n+1}f,\quad \left(\int f_n^2,\,\int\Phi(f_n^2),\,\int\|\nabla f_n\|^2\right)\longrightarrow\left(\int f^2,\,\int\Phi(f^2),\,\int\|\nabla f\|^2\right)\quad (d\mu\text{ in each integral}).
assumptions: Complete real Hilbert space with compatible Borel structure; mu is an arbitrary measure.
C2 f, f and its genuine gradient in L2(mu), Phi(f^2) in L1(mu).

steps.title: Control mass and entropy integrands
steps.text: Use the cutoff range to dominate the mass by f squared. For q=f squared and a=chi squared, the zero-aware product identity and the bound on Phi(a) give an integrable entropy envelope, without dividing by q.
steps.lean: The private entropy_dilation_bound uses Real.negMulLog_mul and the bounds on Real.mul_log.

steps.title: Control the genuine derivative
steps.text: Use the product derivative and the Riesz isometry. Since n+1 is at least one, the uniform first derivative constant K gives the stated integrable envelope. At any fixed x the cutoff is eventually one in an open neighborhood, so the gradients eventually agree there.

steps.title: Pass each integral to the limit
steps.text: Continuity gives a.e. strong measurability. The three integrable envelopes and the pointwise limits give dominated convergence separately; continuity of Phi includes zero.

units.title: Extend compact smooth LSI to the noncompact smooth analytic domain
units.statement: Fix C and a Borel measure on a finite-dimensional real Hilbert space. Assume the inequality with coefficient 2C for all compactly supported smooth real tests, written with Mathlib's totalized Bochner integrals (a nonintegrable integrand has integral zero). Then the same inequality holds with genuine integrable terms for every smooth real f with f and its true gradient in L2 and f squared times its logarithm in L1. No probability, positive mass, sign of f or sign of C is assumed. On the source's probability measures the compact-test premise uses genuine integrals and is the classical function-form LSI.
assumptions: An arbitrary Borel measure on a finite-dimensional complete real Hilbert space; fixed real C.
The compact smooth premise uses totalized integrals on an arbitrary measure. For the source probability law compact continuous tests and their genuine gradient energies are integrable.
The extended test has the stated genuine analytic domain.

steps.title: Apply the premise to valid tests
steps.text: Multiply f by the smooth radial cutoff. Finite dimension gives compact support, not integrability on arbitrary measures. For these particular cutoff products, the mass, entropy and energy envelopes in the shared proof give integrability. No unsupported direct application to f is made.
steps.lean: The cutoff compactness and smoothness API gives the exact tests. The shared cutoff-integral proof bounds all three integrands by actual integrable functions.

steps.title: Pass the inequality with the same constant
steps.text: Use the shared limits for mass, entropy integrand and true gradient energy. Continuity of t log t transfers the normalization even at zero mass. Closedness of real order passes the estimate to the limit without a sign assumption on the fixed coefficient.
steps.lean: cutoff_integral_limits, Real.continuous_mul_log and le_of_tendsto_of_tendsto close the inequality.

units.lean_statement: The compact C-infinity premise is universal with the Mathlib Bochner integral convention; the extended test is smooth and has explicit integrability domains. The source probability case avoids totalization for compact tests.
units.lean_proof: Apply the compact inequality on actual cutoff products and pass all terms through their real limits.
